headline: High: ChatGPT Desktop can ingest files/screenshots while dexter has broad network egress and API access, creating default-path leakage and cascading-action risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can read files, screenshots, clipboard, and connected-app content, so malicious content from dexter outputs could be reinterpreted as instructions if copied into shared artifacts. dexter has autonomous execution and broad API use, making it plausible it can generate attacker-controlled text that ChatGPT Desktop ingests. No direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty stays medium.
conditions: IF dexter writes attacker-controlled instructions into a file that ChatGPT Desktop reads
IF the operator copies dexter output into ChatGPT Desktop clipboard or screenshots
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff between the agents
Use a plain-text intermediary file with a fixed template
Review dexter output before pasting into ChatGPT Desktop
Turn off file ingestion for untrusted dexter artifacts
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to shared artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected IDE code, while dexter handles financial and market data and has broad network egress plus multiple third-party APIs. If the pair shares sensitive inputs, dexter can transmit them off-box by default, creating a realistic leakage path. The interaction is inferred from profiles, not directly observed, so confidence is moderate.
conditions: IF ChatGPT Desktop receives uploaded files or screenshots containing sensitive data
IF dexter is given the same data class and allowed to call external APIs
mitigations: Do not pass sensitive files from ChatGPT Desktop to dexter
Restrict dexter API keys to non-sensitive test data
Use separate workspaces for each agent
Rotate or scope API keys before any shared-data run
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on dexter outbound requests

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop is read-only on filesystem but can access user files and connected-app content; dexter writes to .dexter/scratchpad/ and uses autonomous execution. That creates overlapping mutable-state risk if both are pointed at the same workspace or synced folder. The profiles do not prove a shared directory by default, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to operate on the same synced workspace
IF dexter writes scratchpad artifacts into a directory ChatGPT Desktop also reads
mitigations: Keep dexter scratchpad outside ChatGPT Desktop-visible folders
Use per-agent directories with distinct permissions
Avoid concurrent edits to the same project tree
Check for accidental sync of .dexter/scratchpad
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: dexter’s autonomous execution can turn ChatGPT Desktop output into downstream actions, and ChatGPT Desktop can surface file or app content that dexter may treat as authoritative. Because dexter has broad network/API access, a mistaken or injected ChatGPT output can cascade into external requests or financial-research actions. The pairwise pathway is plausible in default use, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF dexter consumes ChatGPT Desktop output without a verification step
IF ChatGPT Desktop output is used as input to dexter actions or API calls
mitigations: Require human review before dexter acts on ChatGPT output
Add a verification checklist for all ChatGPT-derived facts
Limit dexter to read-only research mode
Separate drafting from execution roles
requires-engineering: implement source-citation validation before actions

E_compliance.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected IDE code, while dexter handles financial data and sends requests to multiple external APIs. That creates a plausible retention and residency mismatch if regulated or sensitive financial data is routed through both systems. The profiles do not specify a concrete jurisdiction conflict, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is processed by both agents
IF either agent logs or retains the shared data longer than the other
mitigations: Classify the data before sharing it
Keep regulated data out of dexter runs
Review retention settings for both tools
Use redacted samples for testing
requires-engineering: document a DPA and retention matrix
